children: Japan's fiscal health concerns will be difficult to clear before year-end due to expectations of mounting defense budgets, says Sony Financial Group economist Takayuki Miyajima. As underlying fiscal risks remain a key driver, the 10-year Japanese government bond yield is expected to keep trading around 3%, he says. "The bond market is increasingly pricing in hopes that the Takaichi administration will adjust its reflationary policy to be more market-friendly, with a focus on whether this sentiment can be sustained," he adds. The 10-year JGB yield is last at 2.880%. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
